explanations: Many new kinds were invented in the 20th century, including radio ones in the 1930s and infrared ones in the 1960s.
The reflecting kind, which uses mirrors to collect and focus light, was invented within a few decades of the first refracting one.
The first known practical ones were refracting, with glass lenses, and were invented in the Netherlands at the beginning of the 17th century.
Originally it was an optical instrument using lenses, curved mirrors, or a combination of both.
It is a device used to observe distant objects by their emission, absorption or reflection of electromagnetic radiation.

sources.excerpt: In the 20th century, many new types of telescopes were invented, including radio telescopes in the 1930s and infrared telescopes in the 1960s.
The reflecting telescope, which uses mirrors to collect and focus light, was invented within a few decades of the first refracting telescope.
The first known practical telescopes were refracting telescopes with glass lenses and were invented in the Netherlands at the beginning of the 17th century.
Originally, it was an optical instrument using lenses, curved mirrors, or a combination of both to observe distant objects – an optical telescope.
A telescope is a device used to observe distant objects by their emission, absorption, or reflection of electromagnetic radiation.
